# dsh-lowtide > 提供 DSH 任务队列、峰谷窗口调度及批次执行结果复核。 ## 研究范围 - **仓库**：[KelaoHu/dsh-lowtide](https://github.com/KelaoHu/dsh-lowtide) - **版本号**：0.2.8（[固定提交 e1f8efa528b8e509c68e294919f6b74d0a17aaeb](https://github.com/KelaoHu/dsh-lowtide/tree/e1f8efa528b8e509c68e294919f6b74d0a17aaeb)） - **版本日期**：2026-11-04（固定提交日期，北京时间；不是包发布日期） ## 结论状态 固定根工程及子包接线的静态核查，未测试实际宿主和价格。 ## 洞察短评 - **用途**：需要延后运行非紧急 DSH 任务并集中验收的开发者。 - **亮点**：[Q01](#research-q01) 把任务队列和跨日窗口纳入固定工作流。 - **思考**：[Q02](#research-q02) 自动等级、窗口和实际计价要分别验收。 - **建议**：[Q04](#research-q04) 将实际请求和账单关联以检查净节省。 采用建议：[Q03](#research-q03) 先核对子包身份和隔离 profile，再按 [Q02](#research-q02) 测试自动等级。 ## 核心贡献 [Q01](#research-q01) 把任务队列和跨日窗口纳入固定工作流。 ## 关键质疑 [Q02](#research-q02) 自动等级、窗口和实际计价要分别验收。 ## 重点创新推演与最小验证 [Q04](#research-q04) 将实际请求和账单关联以检查净节省。 用固定时钟测试跨日、重启、暂停及账单口径。 ## 场景与替代办法 需要延后运行非紧急 DSH 任务并集中验收的开发者。 手工在指定时间启动任务，之后逐项看结果和账单。 ## 依赖与流程 | 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 | |---|---|---|---| | 兼容宿主及 Node | 必需 | 运行可安装子包 | 保留手工调度 | | 模型与权限 | 执行必需 | 完成任务 | 停在队列 | | 独立 profile | 验证必需 | 限定状态单写者 | 避免并行部署 | | 步骤 | 执行者与动作 | 成功判据或失败处理 | |---|---|---| | 准备 | 操作者核对制品与状态路径 | 不直接安装根包 | | 试用 | 保留人工确认并投入惰性任务 | 核对窗口和权限 | | 退出 | 关闭调度并检查活跃任务 | 保留需要的台账 | ## 成本与效果 | 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 | |---|---|---|---| | 首次 | 模型和环境成本未知 | 配置窗口与权限 | 未实测 | | 持续 | 请求与重试费用 | 核对批次 | 价格待对账 | | 恢复 | 停止及重跑费用未知 | 检查任务和写入 | 不盲目重试 | | 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 | |---|---|---| | 调度 | 窗口和批次接线 | 重启及真实可靠性 | | 节省 | 价格窗口提供动机 | 实际账单 | ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：根工程如何组织峰谷批处理，哪些结果需要单独验证？ ### Q01 · 根工程和可安装包的区别是什么？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、功能与机制、贡献与相对优势 #### 完整回答 需要在非工作时段执行低优先级开发任务的用户可把任务放入队列，延后执行并集中验收。根包是私有 workspace 的构建入口，core 与实际可安装的 packages/dsh-lowtide 分开。子包导出宿主和客户端，并声明 bundle patch。具体窗口识别与调度在插件子包，跨午夜窗口按起始日期识别，触发后交给批处理。相比人工按时启动任务，项目提供有状态的窗口与任务队列。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 源码核查**：[package.json:1-22](https://github.com/KelaoHu/dsh-lowtide/blob/e1f8efa528b8e509c68e294919f6b74d0a17aaeb/package.json#L1-L22) 根私有工作区入口

查看原文（17行） ```text * Identity of the batch window currently in progress, keyed by the calendar * day the window STARTED (so a midnight-crossing window cannot run twice) * plus the window's range string — with multiple windows (issue #5) each * window earns its own once-per-occurrence latch. Returns null when `now` * is outside every window. */ export function currentWindowKey(now: Date, window: string | string[], tz?: string): string | null { const list = Array.isArray(window) ? window : [window] const active = activeWindows(now, list, tz) if (active.length === 0) return null const range = active[0] const resolvedTz = tz ?? systemTimeZone() const { start } = parseWindowRange(range) const { minutes } = localParts(now, resolvedTz) const anchor = minutes >= start ? now : addDaysInTz(now, resolvedTz, -1) return `${localDateKey(anchor, resolvedTz)}|${range}|${resolvedTz}` } ```

查看原文（37行） ```text export function startScheduler(ctx: Context, store: LowtideStore, tickMs = 30_000): Scheduler { let running = false let startedAt: Date | null = null let lastWindowKey: string | null = null async function run(forced: boolean): Promise { if (running) return if (!forced && store.config.batch.paused) return const now = new Date() const wins = batchWindowList(store.config.batch) const activeRange = forced ? undefined : activeWindows(now, wins, store.config.batch.tz)[0] if (!forced && activeRange === undefined) { // Outside every window: clear the once-per-window latch so the next // window (possibly the same day after a config change) may run again. if (lastWindowKey !== null) lastWindowKey = null return } const key = activeRange === undefined ? null : currentWindowKey(now, wins, store.config.batch.tz) if (!forced) { if (key !== null && key === lastWindowKey) return if (key !== null) lastWindowKey = key recoverDeferred(store) if (!hasQueuedWork(store)) return } running = true startedAt = new Date() try { const end = forced ? new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 3600_000) : batchWindowEnd(new Date(), wins, store.config.batch.tz) // The report records the window that actually triggered this batch // (forced manual runs label the first configured window, as before). await runBatch(ctx, store, end, forced, activeRange ?? wins[0]) } catch (error) { ctx.logger('lowtide').warn('batch failed: %s', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)) } finally { running = false startedAt = null } ```
#### 缺口 - 未运行宿主排程、跨午夜或重启 **影响**：无法确认重复窗口和实际作业结果 **进一步探讨**：用测试时钟和惰性任务核对多窗口、跨日与重启 ### Q02 · 人工放行及低价运行的边界？ **研究主题**：缺陷与关键质疑、工程质量与复用 #### 完整回答 README 总览写每任务经人工放行，自治等级实际另说明 L3 入队后不逐项确认。需用实际配置区分批确认和全自动。窗口负责限制何时启动，不会因为到了结束时间而自动撤回已开始的操作。预检、预算和权限均需要按实际宿主验证，设置一段窗口也不能决定供应商的真实计价。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 作者声明**：[README.md:54-66](https://github.com/KelaoHu/dsh-lowtide/blob/e1f8efa528b8e509c68e294919f6b74d0a17aaeb/README.md#L54-L66) 总览的人工承诺
查看原文（13行） ````text ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ````
**依据 2 · 作者声明**：[README.md:115-133](https://github.com/KelaoHu/dsh-lowtide/blob/e1f8efa528b8e509c68e294919f6b74d0a17aaeb/README.md#L115-L133) 不同自治等级与作者预检说明
查看原文（19行） ```text ## Three autonomy levels - **L1 per-task**: every task needs your individual ✓. Use it early on, or when the repo is precious. - **L2 batch** (default): tasks wait in review; a gate card appears 30 minutes before the batch and releases everything at once; no release, no run. The daily driver. - **L3 full-auto**: filed tasks queue immediately and run in the sandbox at off-peak, zero confirmations (switching asks twice). Built for always-on servers. Individual tasks can override the global level in the ticket modal. ## Architecture: how it runs while you're away Letting an agent run batch jobs while you sleep is a big ask. Four layers underneath make it safe. **The Cordis microkernel.** dsh runs on the Cordis microkernel plugin ecosystem: every capability is a plugin, and plugins talk through service injection rather than direct dependency. lowtide's host half is a set of well-behaved Cordis services — routes, scheduler, state machine — each doing its own job, registered into the kernel, starting with the harness, uninstalling cleanly. In plain words: it's not a skin stapled onto dsh; it's an organ grown inside the kernel. **Two faces, one artifact.** The host half (Node.js) owns scheduling, execution, and the ledger; the browser half (React) owns every pixel. One build produces both — and since dsh Desktop's GUI is itself web-rendered, desktop and web need no separate branches. Same bytes, same behavior. **A platform-agnostic core.** `lowtide-core` holds the window model, price tables, the billing formula, queue digest, ledger, and batch-window math — all pure functions that touch zero dsh APIs, shipped as their own package with their own tests. The practical payoff: the core has been hammered by 44 pure-function unit tests, and if you ever port lowtide to another agent framework, this package lifts out intact. **Defense in depth.** Five preflight gates (is the workspace still there, did git HEAD move, do the locked-file sha256s match, does the window fit, is there budget left) — fail any one and the task goes stale or defers; never a blind run. Three sandbox presets with approval set to never — unattended means nobody is there to click "allow", so what's permitted is decided before the run starts. The state file is written atomically and rolls back to a backup if corrupted. HTTP routes only accept same-origin requests from this machine. ```

The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ```
